title.narrative: Responding to Gender Based Violence (GBV) Survivors, Vulnerable Women and Girls in Contested Areas of Wolkayt, Tsegede and Humera Woredas

description.narrative: ltpgtA rapid need assessment has been conducted in April 2025 by Center of Concern (CoC) which shows that the prevalence of gender-based violence (GBV) risks and cases in the conflict-affected woredas of Wolkayt, Tsegede, and Humera is alarmingly high. Women and girls in these areas face heightened risks of abduction, sexual violence, physical harm, rape, and denial of properties. Despite the high prevalence of GBV risks, response and protection services remain inadequate due to several factors. Many health facilities are damaged from conflict, limiting access to essential health services for women and girls. There is a lack of GBV case management and there no One-Stop Center or Women and Girls Safe Space in targeted areas. Additionally, MHPSS services are insufficient, and there is a lack of awareness-raising efforts on GBV prevention and management in the community. Furthermore, frontline staff and health professionals have not received the necessary training on GBV case management.ltbrgtIn response to these urgent needs, CoC proposes a project titled "Responding to Gender based Violence (GBV) Survivors, Vulnerable Women and Girls in the contested areas of Wolkayt, Tsegede and Humera". The overarching objective of this 7-month project is to provide comprehensive protection services, mitigate GBV risks, and support the recovery and resilience of those affected. The project will address the multifaceted needs of survivors through an integrated approach encompassing GBV case management, MHPSS, and essential sexual and reproductive health services. Key activities include:ltbrgt Provision of life-saving GBV response services, including case management, MHPSS, and referral services. ltbrgt Establishing Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS)ltbrgt Training and capacity building of frontline service providers, including healthcare workers, social workers, police, and community leaders on GBV response, referral pathways, and survivor-centered approachesltbrgt Community-based awareness and risk mitigation initiatives, including information sessions on GBV prevention, reporting mechanisms, and the availability of services.ltbrgt Strengthening referral pathways to ensure timely and safe access to multi-sectoral support including health, legal, psychosocial, and protection services. ltbrgtBy implementing these activities, the project will contribute to reducing protection risks for women and girls and ensuring access to life-saving protection services. This project will benefit 16,027 (womengt18 =8,003, Girls lt18gt18=3,518)lt/pgt
